items.text: The board has 64 squares. Columns are files, lettered a to h from left to right. Rows are ranks, numbered 1 to 8 from White's side. A square is named file first, then rank: e4 is file e, rank 4. The letters and numbers are printed round the edge of every board here.

items.prompt: Tap the square e4.
items.explain: e4 is on file e, the fifth from the left, and rank 4, the fourth row up from White's side.

items.prompt: Tap the square a1.
items.explain: a1 is White's bottom-left corner: file a, rank 1.

items.text: At the start, White's pieces fill ranks 1 and 2 and Black's fill ranks 7 and 8. Each player has a light square in the bottom-right corner.

items.prompt: Tap the square h8.
items.explain: h8 is the top-right corner from White's side: the last file and the last rank.

items.prompt: Tap the square d5.
items.explain: Find file d along the bottom, then go up to rank 5.

items.prompt: Tap the square g2.
items.explain: File g is second from the right, and rank 2 is where White's pawns start.

items.text: The rook moves in straight lines: up, down, left or right, as far as it likes, until something is in the way.

items.prompt: Tap the furthest square the rook can reach in each direction.
items.explain: Up, the rook stops at d5 before your own pawn. Down it runs to d1, right it stops at e4, and left it can take the pawn on b4 but go no further.

items.prompt: Move the rook to d8.
items.explain: Straight up the d-file. Nothing is in the way, so the rook goes all the way.

items.text: The bishop moves diagonally, as far as it likes. A bishop stays on squares of one colour all game.

items.prompt: Tap the furthest square the bishop can reach along each diagonal.
items.explain: Up-left it can take the pawn on b6. Up-right it runs to h8, down-left to a1, and down-right your own pawn on f2 stops it at e3.

items.prompt: Move the bishop to a7.
items.explain: Diagonally up and to the left: d4, c5, b6, a7.

items.text: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop together: straight or diagonal, as far as she likes. She is the strongest piece.

items.prompt: Tap the furthest square the queen can reach in each direction.
items.explain: Hemmed in by her own pawns, the queen can still run up to d8 and down to d1, and take either black pawn on c5 or e5.

items.prompt: Move the queen to a4.
items.explain: Straight along rank 4: d4, c4, b4, a4.

items.text: The king moves one square in any direction. He may never step onto a square an enemy piece attacks.

items.prompt: Tap every square the king can move to.
items.explain: The rook on d2 attacks the whole d-file, so the king can't step onto d3, d4 or d5. Five squares are left.

items.prompt: Step the king to f5.
items.explain: One step diagonally, up and to the right. Kings only ever move one square.

items.text: The knight moves in an L: two squares one way, then one square to the side. It is the only piece that jumps over others.

items.prompt: Tap every square the knight can move to.
items.explain: From the middle a knight has eight squares, every one an L-shape away.

items.prompt: Tap every square the knight can move to.
items.explain: In the corner a knight has only two squares. Knights are strongest in the middle.

items.prompt: Pawns all round it. Tap every square the knight can move to.
items.explain: Still all eight: the knight jumps straight over the pawns.

items.prompt: Move the knight to f5.
items.explain: Two squares to the right and one up: that L takes the knight from d4 to f5.

items.text: Pawns move straight forward one square, or two on their very first move. They capture differently: one square diagonally forward.

items.prompt: Tap the furthest square this pawn can move to.
items.explain: On its very first move a pawn may go two squares: e2 to e4.

items.prompt: Tap every square this pawn can move to.
items.explain: Forward to e5, or take diagonally on d5 or f5. Pawns take on the diagonal, never straight ahead.

items.text: A pawn can't move forward if anything stands in front of it, friend or enemy. It can't take straight ahead either.

items.prompt: Take the black pawn with your pawn.
items.explain: Pawn takes on d5: one square diagonally forward.

items.prompt: Push the pawn to the last rank.
items.explain: A pawn that reaches the far side becomes a queen. That's promotion, and it's how one pawn can win a game.

items.text: To capture, move onto an enemy piece's square: it leaves the board. Pieces are worth points: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king is never captured.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece your rook can capture.
items.explain: The rook reaches the bishop on b4, the queen on d2, the knight on d6 and the pawn on g4.

items.prompt: Take the most valuable piece you can.
items.explain: Rook takes the queen on d2: 9 points for a piece worth 5. Look at what every capture wins before you choose.

items.text: Before you take, check whether the piece is defended. Here the pawn on e4 is guarded by the pawn on d5: take it with your queen and the queen is lost.

items.prompt: Take the piece that nothing defends.
items.explain: The knight on a4 is free. Take the bishop on g4 instead and the pawn on h5 takes your queen.

items.text: When a piece attacks the king, the king is in check. The player in check must end it straight away: move the king, block the attack, or capture the attacker.

items.prompt: True or false: the black king is in check.
items.explain: The rook on e1 looks straight up the e-file at the king on e8.

items.prompt: True or false: the black king is in check.
items.explain: The rook is on the d-file and the king is on e8. Nothing attacks it.

items.prompt: Give check with the rook.
items.explain: Rook to e1 or rook to a8: either way the rook attacks the king. That's check.

items.prompt: Your king is in check from the rook. Get out of check.
items.explain: Step off the g-file, out of the rook's line. Moving along the file, like to g2, stays in check.

items.prompt: You're in check. End it by capturing the piece giving it.
items.explain: Nothing defends the queen on f2: take it with the rook or the king. Capturing the attacker ends the check and wins the queen.

items.text: Checkmate is check with no way out: the king can't move, the attack can't be blocked, and the attacker can't be taken. Checkmate wins the game.

items.prompt: True or false: Black is checkmated.
items.explain: The rook on d8 checks along the back rank, Black's own pawns block every escape, and nothing can take or block the rook.

items.prompt: True or false: Black is checkmated.
items.explain: It's check, but the king can step to h7, where the h-pawn used to stand. Mate needs no way out at all.

items.prompt: Checkmate in one move.
items.explain: Rook to d8 is checkmate: the black pawns trap their own king on the back rank.

items.prompt: Checkmate in one move.
items.explain: Queen to b7, guarded by your king, or queen to h8 along the back rank: either way the black king has nowhere to go.

items.prompt: Checkmate in one move.
items.explain: Rook to a8 covers the whole back rank, and your king guards g7 and h7.
